title: Fix saturated orbit depth visualization
objective: Investigate and fix the flashlight orbit collection depth PNG/video visualization still appearing nearly single-color/saturated after stable per-setting normalization. Preserve raw metric .npy depth outputs.
instructions: Do not perform any Git commit or Git operation beyond reading status/diffs if needed; Tower policy now requires explicit user authorization for commits.

Review examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py and the existing depth visualization helpers. Determine why per-setting finite min/max can still produce nearly single-color viridis output, especially if outliers or huge far-plane values dominate the range.

Implement a practical visualization fix for rendered depth PNGs/videos while preserving raw .npy metric depth exactly. Prefer robust configurable depth visualization bounds such as finite percentile clipping and/or optional explicit min/max CLI args; keep defaults useful for active-illumination orbit videos.
Update docs and tests for any new options or behavior. Keep changes lean and consistent with existing script style.
Run focused non-simulator validation: unit tests, py_compile, and helper smoke tests for saturation/contrast behavior. Do not require live SPEAR validation.
definition_of_done: Depth visualization has robust contrast by default for orbit videos, raw .npy output remains unmodified, docs/tests reflect behavior, and no commit is created.
